title: Flip one bit of the message
hook: Change a message by a single bit. How much of its SHA-256 hash moves?

knows: a hash maps data to a fixed-size output
letters are stored as 8 bits each
doesNotKnow: that a good hash output looks unrelated after a tiny input change (the avalanche effect)

misconception: Similar inputs give similar hashes, so a hash is a rough fingerprint of the content.
objective: The learner can explain that flipping one input bit changes about half (about 128 of 256) of SHA-256's output bits, so similar messages get unrelated hashes and a message cannot be nudged toward a target hash.

claims.text: SHA-256 turns any message into 256 bits.
claims.source: NIST FIPS 180-4, Secure Hash Standard (2015), section 6.2: SHA-256 message digest is 256 bits.

claims.text: Flipping one bit of the message changes about half of the 256 output bits, about 128 on average, not a handful.
claims.source: Builder ran 1,000 random one-bit flips of random 3-byte messages through sha256.ts in Node: mean 127.7 changed bits, min 103, max 157. On the stage's QA path (bits 1-16 of 'cat', flipped in turn) the counts were 129, 112, 129, 131, 137, 122, 135, 123, 127, 125, 127, 136, 117, 132, 127, 126.

claims.text: The stage computes a real SHA-256 of the 3-letter message (8 bits per letter) on every tap.
claims.source: sha256.ts in the lesson folder. Builder checked: 'abc' gives ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad (FIPS 180-4 example) and 200 further inputs match Node's crypto.createHash('sha256'). Letters are ASCII bytes ('c' = 0x63).

claims.text: A good hash is built so that each output bit flips with a chance of about one half, like a coin toss, when any input bit changes.
claims.source: Strict avalanche criterion: Webster and Tavares, 'On the Design of S-Boxes', CRYPTO '85. Expected 256 x 1/2 = 128 matches c2's simulation.

claims.text: So similar messages do not get similar hashes, and a message cannot be nudged toward a chosen hash bit by bit.
claims.source: Preimage resistance as a design goal of SHA-2: NIST SP 800-107 Rev. 1 (2012), section 4.1; the avalanche result (c2) is why small edits give no partial progress. Stated as a design property, not a proof.

recall.question: Two files differ in a single character. You compare their SHA-256 hashes bit by bit. What do you expect?
options: About half of the bits differ
recall.why: A good hash makes every output bit flip with about a coin-toss chance when anything changes, so about 128 of 256 bits differ: the hashes look unrelated.
